item.title: Curriculum Vitae
item.description:
Golam Mohiuddin Shaifullah

Postdoctoral researcher in the G. Occhialini Department of Physics at the University of Milano-Bicocca. I am a radio astronomer studying pulsars: the rapidly rotating, collapsed remnants of supernovae. I use these objects to search for nanohertz gravitational waves and to study ionised gas in the Milky Way and the Solar system.

golam.shaifullah@unimib.it · golam.shaifullah@gmail.com
Milan, Italy

Appointments

2020–present — Postdoctoral Researcher
G. Occhialini Department of Physics, University of Milano-Bicocca, Milan, Italy. Supervisor: Prof. Alberto Sesana.

2017–2020 — Postdoctoral Researcher
ASTRON, the Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy, Dwingeloo, the Netherlands.

2012–2013 — Senior Research Fellow
Department of Electronic Science, University of Pune, Pune, India.

2010–2012 — Junior Research Fellow
Department of Electronic Science, University of Pune, Pune, India.

Education

2013–2017 — Dr. rer. nat. (PhD), Physics
Universität Bielefeld, Germany. Thesis: Timing and properties of recycled pulsars.

2008–2010 — MSc, Physics (First Class)
Fergusson College, University of Pune, India.

2005–2008 — BSc, Physics, Electronics and Mathematics (First Class)
St Joseph’s College, Bangalore University, India.

Research

My research centres on creating and analysing high-precision pulsar-timing datasets. Pulsar timing arrays use pulsars distributed across the Galaxy to detect very-low-frequency gravitational waves, including signals produced by inspiralling supermassive black-hole binaries. I combine observations from telescopes and instruments used by the European and International Pulsar Timing Arrays, study propagation through the interstellar medium, and improve models that mitigate those effects.

I also study pulsars over a broad range of radio frequencies using facilities including Arecibo, Effelsberg, the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope, Parkes, LOFAR, NenuFAR and MeerKAT.

Teaching and supervision

  • Supervision and co-supervision of MSc, PhD and BSc projects in pulsar timing, gravitational-wave searches, scintillation, astrometry and the interstellar medium at Milano-Bicocca, Nijmegen, Leiden and Bielefeld.
  • Designed and conducted MSc laboratory courses at the Department of Electronic Science, University of Pune (2010–2013).
  • Designed and conducted an MSc bridge course in electronics (2010–2011).
  • Taught an Applied Electrodynamics laboratory at the Centre for Excellence in Basic Sciences, Mumbai University (2010–2011).
  • Tutorials on Enterprise, PSRCHIVE, Tempo2 and regression analysis.

Service and memberships

  • 2024–present: Member, Gravitational Wave International Committee.
  • 2022–2024: Executive Committee member, European Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2022–present: General Secretary, Gravitational-Wave Early Career Scientists.
  • 2022–present: Co-chair, Data Combination Working Group, International Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2021–present: Founder chair, PTA Early Career Scientists Working Group.
  • 2017–present: Chair, Timing and IISM working groups, European Pulsar Timing Array.
  • Member of the NenuFAR Pulsar Key Project, MeerTIME, COSPAR-ISWAT and the LISA Astro Working Group.

Grants, awards and professional activity

  • 2013–2017: MPG Stipendiat, Max Planck Society, Germany.
  • 2009: Summer Research Fellowship, Indian Academy of Sciences, India.
  • Principal investigator or co-investigator on successful observing proposals with Effelsberg, Arecibo, LOFAR, GMRT and Parkes, and member of key science programmes at MeerKAT and NenuFAR.
  • Referee for The Astrophysical Journal, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, and Science China Physics, Mechanics & Astronomy; proposal reviewer for the GMRT Time Allocation Committee.

Publications and talks

The complete, automatically maintained lists are available on the publications page and in the [talks section] (/en/#talks) of this website.

Languages

English (first language); Hindi and Bengali (advanced); Marathi (intermediate); German, Dutch and Italian (basic).
